clue.text: Shock inclusion of exiled premier brings call for dismissal

indicators.note: the shock word includes, or takes inside it, the next piece

parts.note: to shock someone is to appal them

indicators.note: premier means first, so only the opening letter of exiled is used

explanation.surface: An outraged inclusion of a banished prime minister prompts demands that someone be sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inclusion of' puts E, the first letter of 'exiled', inside APPAL. In cricket the fielders appeal to the umpire to give a batter out.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, the fielding side's shout to the umpire asking for a batter to be given out is called by this name.

clue.text: Boeing, perhaps, crosses sea via Torbay

indicators.note: the run of letters crosses the word gaps in the phrase that follows, sitting inside it

explanation.surface: A Boeing jet flies over the sea on its way to Torbay, a Devon resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Boeing looks like the aircraft, but here it means William Boeing, the man who founded the company and flew planes himself. The answer is spread across 'seA VIA TORbay'.
explanation.definitionFit: William Boeing, founder of the aircraft company, was himself a pilot, so he is one example of a flyer of planes.

clue.text: See 4
Spaniel uprooted plants

indicators.note: pulled up and thrown about, so the letters of the dog's name are disturbed

explanation.surface: A spaniel digs up the plants in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uprooted' sits naturally with 'plants' in the picture, but it is the anagram signal working on 'Spaniel'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpines are small mountain flowers grown in rock gardens, a group of plants.

clue.text: It affects sound of revolutionary propagandist broadcasting traffic

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns round, so the propagandist's name is read backwards

parts.note: Lord Haw-Haw was the nickname of William Joyce, who broadcast Nazi propaganda to Britain in the Second World War

indicators.note: broadcasting means spoken on air, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: to traffic in goods is to peddle them

explanation.surface: A rebel propagandist on the radio talks about the traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' reverses HAWHAW into WAHWAH, and 'broadcasting' signals that PEDAL sounds like PEDDLE. The answer covers this light and 2-down.
explanation.definitionFit: A guitarist's foot-operated effects unit sweeps the tone up and down, so it changes the instrument's sound.

clue.text: A base unit is spoiled, if ends are detached

indicators.note: the two end letters of the spoiling word are cut off

parts.note: a spoiled child has been pampered

explanation.surface: A unit at a military base has gone to the bad, if its far parts break away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'If ends are detached' removes the first and last letters, P and D. HAMPERED or TAMPERED for 'spoiled' works just as well.
explanation.definitionFit: The ampere, the unit of electric current, is one of the seven SI base units of measurement.

clue.text: Socially circulate computer malware around region of South Africa

indicators.note: the malware word goes around the region, which sits inside it

parts.note: a worm is self-copying malicious software that spreads across networks
the Karoo is a large semi-desert region of South Africa

explanation.surface: Software that spreads infection circulates around a part of South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The Karoo is a vast dry plateau in South Africa's interior; the malware word is split around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To move round a party talking to many guests is an idiom for mingling socially.

clue.text: It cushions joint when straddling animal

indicators.note: straddling means sitting astride, so the joint word sits around the animal

parts.note: the hock is the joint in a horse's hind leg
an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: Something softens the impact on a leg joint when you sit astride a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: A hassock is a firm cushion for kneeling on in church, hence 'It cushions'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hassock is a padded kneeling cushion in church, so it is a thing that softens a kneeler's weight.

clue.text: One flying up smooth cloth to Sweden a bit at a time

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a bird is a thing that flies
to sand wood is to smooth it
drab is a dull brown woollen cloth
S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

explanation.surface: Someone flies up to smooth out a cloth bound for Sweden, piece by piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' reverses BIRD to give DRIB.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming in small scattered amounts, a little now and a little later, is what this idiom describes.

clue.text: Chinook hit airport equipment

parts.note: the chinook is a warm dry wind blowing down the Rocky Mountains
to sock someone is to hit them

explanation.surface: A Chinook helicopter struck a piece of airport kit.
explanation.walkthrough: Chinook looks like the military helicopter, but here it is the North American wind. The answer covers this light and 16-across.
explanation.definitionFit: A fabric cone on a pole showing pilots the direction and strength of the wind is standard kit at an airfield.

clue.text: Rapper has a new way to say the same things

definitions.text: way to say the same things

indicators.note: new means remade, so these letters are formed afresh

explanation.surface: A rapper finds a fresh way of putting old lyrics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' is the anagram signal working on 'Rapper has a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Restating a text in different words while keeping its meaning is a rewording, a way of saying it again.

clue.text: Knocked off vestment with pole

parts.note: a stole is a long strip worn round the neck by a priest
N stands for the north pole

explanation.surface: A priest's vestment was knocked over by a pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked off' is slang for stolen, not knocked over.
explanation.definitionFit: Knocked off is British slang for pinched or taken without paying, a synonym for thieved.

clue.text: Dig first and then pop back to the country

parts.note: a dig is a cutting remark, a barb

indicators.note: back means the drink word is read in reverse

parts.note: pop is a fizzy drink, soda

explanation.surface: Instructions to dig the ground before nipping back to the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reverses SODA to give ADOS. 'The country' is not the countryside but a nation, the Caribbean island state.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbados is an island nation in the Caribbean, an independent state.

clue.text: Shopkeeper and master criminal

indicators.note: criminal means bent or crooked, so the letters are bent out of shape

explanation.surface: A shop owner who is also a mastermind of crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like a noun after 'master', but it is the anagram signal working on 'and master'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman is someone who sells goods, a dealer or retailer keeping a store.

clue.text: Old tales by posh boy keen to depart for Spain

indicators.note: the keen word leaves and the Spain letter takes its place

parts.note: David Cameron, the Eton-educated UK prime minister, was dismissed by critics as a posh boy
keen means avid
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Ancient stories from a well-to-do lad eager to head off to Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To depart for' takes AVID out of DAVIDCAMERON and puts E in its place, leaving DECAMERON.
explanation.definitionFit: Boccaccio's fourteenth-century collection of a hundred stories is a famous book of medieval narratives.

clue.text: Celibate for one day last week

parts.note: Mon is short for Monday

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the word week

explanation.surface: One gives up sex for a day in the final week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For one' marks the answer as an example of a celibate rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A man in a religious order who has taken vows of chastity is an example of a celibate person.

clue.text: See 9
1 of 5 in school gives support for spire

indicators.note: in places the quintuplet inside the school word

parts.note: a quin is one of five babies born together, a quintuplet

explanation.surface: One quintuplet at school is helping hold up the church spire.
explanation.walkthrough: A squinch is a term from church architecture: an arch built across the inside corner of a square tower.
explanation.definitionFit: A squinch is an arch across a tower's corner that carries an octagonal spire or dome, a structural support.

clue.text: Stir navy dye glutton left for decoration

parts.note: a stir is a fuss or commotion, an ado
RN is the Royal Navy

indicators.note: left means departed, so the glutton word is taken out

parts.note: a pigment is a colouring substance
a pig is a glutton

explanation.surface: Instructions to stir navy dye, with a greedy eater gone, for decorating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' takes PIG out of PIGMENT, leaving MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornament or embellishment added to make something attractive is decoration.

clue.text: Harsh treatment at ring leader's trial, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the letters are judged by their sound

parts.note: the leader of ring is R, and a trial is an ordeal, so together they give R plus ORDEAL

explanation.surface: A ringleader gets a rough deal at the trial, so we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: R plus ORDEAL, said in a non-rhotic British accent where the R of OR is silent, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfair or harsh handling of someone is an idiom for a bad bargain, rotten luck.

clue.text: Disbelief expressed — Tory leader behind the bid

parts.note: No! is what someone exclaims in disbelief

indicators.note: the leader of Tory is its first letter

parts.note: the rump is the behind, the backside

explanation.surface: Disbelief greets the news that a Tory leader is behind the takeover bid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The bid' is not a takeover but a call in bridge, where a hand may be played with no suit as trumps.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, a call to play the hand without any trump suit is one of the contract bids.

clue.text: Trendy art movement's lost manuscript raised spirits

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: lost means the art movement has lost a piece

parts.note: Cubism was the art movement of Picasso and Braque

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the manuscript abbreviation is turned upwards

explanation.surface: A fashionable art movement lost a manuscript, which lifted their spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' turns MS into SM, and 'lost' removes SM from the end of CUBISM, leaving CUBI.
explanation.definitionFit: Incubi are male demons of folklore who were said to visit sleeping women, a kind of evil spirit.

clue.text: Old archbishop takes in second pilgrim en route to Canterbury

indicators.note: takes in means contains, so the archbishop's name holds the second

parts.note: John Bird Sumner was Archbishop of Canterbury in the nineteenth century
mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A former archbishop welcomes a second pilgrim walking to Canterbury.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers to the Summoner, one of the pilgrims who tells a story in Chaucer's Canterbury Tales.
explanation.definitionFit: The Summoner is a character in Chaucer's Canterbury Tales, one of the travellers riding to the shrine.

clue.text: With inquiring expression, insert key to reveal treasure

indicators.note: insert means put the key inside the inquiring expression

parts.note: Eh? is said when asking a question
Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: With a puzzled look, someone puts in a key to unlock the hidden hoard.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasure as a noun means riches, money and valuables, which is a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Marble passageway

definitions.meaning: a large marble used in the children's game of marbles

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a big playing marble and a narrow passage between houses.

clue.text: Weave rug inside? Woman up to it, without doubt

indicators.note: inside means the rearranged rug goes within the other pieces

parts.note: Una is a woman's name
to be up to it is to be able

indicators.note: to weave is to interlace, so the letters of the floor covering are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman asks whether to weave a rug inside, and she is certainly capable.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark after 'inside' marks the surface break: the rug's letters are placed within the woman and the ability words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beyond dispute that nobody could contest is certain, without doubt.

clue.text: Whack head fleeing brute

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, of the whacking word runs off

parts.note: to clout someone is to whack them

explanation.surface: Someone thumps an oaf, who runs away headfirst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head fleeing' removes C, the first letter of CLOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A lout is a rough, uncouth and aggressive man, a thug or brute.

clue.text: Woman purchased a plant

parts.note: hen is slang for a woman
to bite at a lie is to buy it, so purchased gives the past tense bit

explanation.surface: A woman bought a pot plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purchased' looks like shopping, but it is in the sense of believing a story: you bought it, you bit.
explanation.definitionFit: Henbit is a dead-nettle, a low weed with purple flowers, so it is one kind of plant.

clue.text: Emphasise power with shot on court

parts.note: P is the symbol for power
a lay-up is a short basketball shot played off the backboard

explanation.surface: A powerful shot on the tennis court gives extra stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests tennis, but the shot is in basketball.
explanation.definitionFit: To stress or highlight something is a phrasal verb meaning to give it prominence.
